key_insight: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting (CoPE) adds multi-step action forecasting to agent RL so the policy learns from intermediate trajectories, not just a terminal reward.
engineering_relevance: This can improve sample efficiency and training stability for language agents in long-horizon tasks without adding inference-time cost or extra models.
method: Train on successful on-policy trajectories and supervise the policy to predict the next action sequence from prior histories.
Combine action forecasting with standard acting so both objectives shape a shared backbone during training.
Use a single policy backbone only; inference remains one-step action selection with no overhead.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on five benchmarks (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, τ²-bench, and AppWorld), CoPE outperforms GRPO and predictive-auxiliary RL baselines, with up to 1.9× higher sample efficiency than ECHO and 2.0× higher than GRPO on ScienceWorld.
watch_item: The approach depends on successful on-policy trajectories and careful construction of multi-step action targets, which may be challenging in sparse-reward or noisy environments.
paper_title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
